title: Non-league team-mates told to find new clubs after ‘inexcusable’ on-pitch altercation
content:
Two team-mates from tier eight side Rushden & Diamonds have been told to find new clubs after being sent off for an on-pitch altercation

Bruno Andrade, 32, and fellow forward Tyler Winters, 20, were dismissed in the 21st minute of Saturday’s Northern Premier League Midlands Division fixture against Loughborough Students in what was described as a “nightmare” and “inexcusable” incident.

Rushden & Diamonds confirmed the two players would not represent the club for the remainder of the 2025-26 campaign and were “free to pursue opportunities” elsewhere following an internal review of the incident.

“The actions seen during the incident do not reflect the standards we expect of those representing AFC Rushden & Diamonds,” a club statement read. “As a fan-owned, community-driven club, we have a responsibility to uphold those standards and to act when they are not met.

“On this occasion, the issue extends beyond on-pitch contribution.

“We recognise that football is an emotional game, but incidents of this nature require a clear and considered response in order to protect the integrity and reputation of the club.”

The Northamptonshire side were trailing 1-0 when they were reduced to nine players mid-way through the first half, with manager Elliot Sandy explaining at full time that a disagreement between Andrade and Winters had become physical. Rushden & Diamonds’ live commentary feed stated the two players had clashed earlier in the match before the sending off.

“I have never seen anything quite like this,” the club’s live text feed read. “A coming together between Bruno and Tyler, not the first of the game, results in the two players being shown straight red cards! It’s an absolute nightmare for Diamonds who now have 9 men and no forwards!”

Andrade thanked the club and supporters on X, adding: “Sorry it’s ended this way”. Winters also thanked his team-mates and the club’s fans, adding: “I tried to remove myself from the situation long before the red but got told to carry on.”

Andrade, who spent a number of years in in the English Football League (EFL) across spells with clubs including Queens Park Rangers, Salford City and Lincoln City, was captaining Rushden & Diamonds during Saturday’s fixture, having joined the club in the summer. Winters also joined the club in the summer, and both players participate in the celebrity-backed six-aside Baller League.

“They had a bit of a disagreement on the pitch and culminated in those two coming together,” manager Sandy told the club’s in-house media at full time.

“The linesman said there was a bit of hands and stuff between the two of them, and two red cards. They’ve let themselves down, let the club down, they’ve let their teammates down. It’s inexcusable.”

Rushden & Diamonds were beaten 3-0 by Loughborough on Saturday to leave the club ninth, five points outside the play-offs.
